column1: # Allowed callers of guarded kernel functions: GitHub issue #1107 (folds
# each kernel object and, for every row, refuses a function outside the
# allowed set that calls the guarded function or takes it as a value, and
# refuses a table in which an allowed caller no longer calls it.
# Columns (tab-separated): check name, guarded function, allowed callers as
# comma-separated file:function, issue, reason (printed on a refusal).
# Adding a caller is a review: write why it may name the function here.

column5: TPIDR_EL1 is read only by cpu_authority.tkb's preempt_slot(); any other caller is a second, unreviewed way to name the current CPU
the exec inode is stored only from a SyscallExecInode by syscall.tkb's syscall_exec_inode_store; any other caller would store an inode the format check never judged
dc civac is DDB-only: rp1_gem.tkb's kernel_net_rx_frame_pending() is its one reviewed caller; any other caller is cache maintenance outside the DMA owners

the QEMU virt (no bus offset) address of a DMA span is given only to a virtio-mmio queue or descriptor by these reviewed writers; a new caller is a new device-visible address, reviewed against dma_address.tkb's rule

the RP1 bus address of a DMA span is given only to a GEM or xHCI descriptor or register by these reviewed writers; a new caller is a new device-visible address, reviewed against dma_address.tkb's rule
a DMA span's CPU physical address is taken only for rp1_gem's DDB RX look (#959, #1095); any other caller is CPU access to a device region outside its owner
PSTATE.PAN is cleared only by the linear UserAccessWindow, whose closer is owed on every path; any other caller opens user memory to EL1 with nothing to close it
PSTATE.PAN is set again only by the window closer that consumes the UserAccessWindow

a user-access window is opened only by the user_memory.tkb accessors, each around one access to a range already validated (and its COW pages resolved); any other opener is an EL1 user access outside a checked range
